**My thinking:**

I've been doing wheat-maize rotation on this land for years. My 6 mu all goes into the rotation — wheat in winter, maize in summer, back to back. That's how everyone farms here in Quzhou, and it makes sense: two harvests a year, steady income, steady food for my family of seven.

For **wheat**, I'll plant in early October like always. I buy improved seed from the township supply station — the hybrid-style improved varieties give me more reliable yields than old seed, and I've seen the difference. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest to work in the crop residue. I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting, then come back with urea at jointing stage in March. I irrigate four times: once before winter sets in to protect roots, once at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain fill if the well water holds. I spray herbicide in spring when the broadleafs come up, and I spray once at heading for aphids and powdery mildew. I expect around 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For **maize**, I go straight into the field after wheat harvest in mid-June — no tillage, just direct seed into the stubble. Saves time and moisture both. I use hybrid seed, the kind sold at the agricultural materials shop in town. I put down some base compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress with urea at the big bell stage. I irrigate at planting if it's dry, again at silking, and maybe a third time if there's a drought mid-season. I spray herbicide early post-emergence, and I watch for corn borers and spray once if I see them. I expect around 550 kg per mu from maize.
